newsitem.title: UK: UK adviser Minford sees no sign of overheating.
newsitem.headline: UK adviser Minford sees no sign of overheating.

text.p: Patrick Minford, a member of the UK Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers, challenged the view of his colleagues on the panel that the economy was on the verge of overheating.
"The idea that we are on the verge of an unsustainable boom sems to me to be basically fanciful," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.

Minford, who has repeatedly called for lower interest rates and lower taxes, said Britain already had the highest real interest rates in Europe by a large margin and rates were also higher than in the U.S., which was at a more mature stage of its recovery.
Monetary policy was the most potent reason for the rise in sterling.
A further tightening of monetary policy would be "highly inappropriate for an economy which has got a great deal of excess capacity in the labour market," Minford said.

Taking issue with colleagues such as Gavyn Davies over the state of the public finances, Minford said: "The longer-term financial situation is much better than Gavyn Davies has painted it. That implies...there was the scope in this budget to cut marginal tax rates much more."
"The fundamental finances of the public sector...are as sound as in the whole of the OECD, if you do the sums looking forward and including pensions."
